source.title: UniMax: Fairer and more Effective Language Sampling for Large-Scale Multilingual Pretraining
source.authors: Hyung Won Chung; Noah Constant; Xavier García; Adam Roberts; Yi Tay; Sharan Narang; O. Firat

record.tranche_reason: The study measures held-out pretraining loss and downstream results across model sizes and language-sampling setups. It reports overfitting under repeated-data sampling at larger scales, but does not fit or test power laws or compute-optimal parameter/token allocations.
record.gate_note: The study does not fit loss-versus-parameter, token, or compute power laws, test small-run extrapolation, or determine compute-optimal allocations. Its held-out loss curves do report repeated-data overfitting, and its downstream evaluations report results across model sizes. Cited claims from other work about repeated data are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The study's own downstream evaluations bear on V6 in multilingual encoder-decoder models: scores improve across tested model sizes, with an explicitly reported exception caused by training instability. It does not test power-law forms, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, architecture invariance, or fit-dependent scaling laws. Repetition-induced overfitting alone does not establish V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors conclude that UniMax provides more uniform language coverage while limiting repetition, performs well across benchmarks and scales up to 13B parameters, and avoids the overfitting observed in the displayed temperature-sampling curves. Gains at still larger sizes are an expectation, not a demonstrated result; the study uses one pretraining paradigm and reports an unstable umT5-Large exception.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares multilingual language-sampling strategies and evaluates their effects on held-out loss and downstream tasks; it does not reproduce the scaling-law fitting or compute-optimal allocation methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Held-out loss overfitting varies with sampling strategy, model size, language, and training duration; UniMax max-epoch cap and character budget are also ablated.

fits_no_version.finding: Yoruba held-out loss overfits weakly at XL and conspicuously at XXL under temperature 3.33; a longer Large run overfits after approximately 300,000 steps. UniMax shows no reported overfitting in these curves.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In this multilingual span-corruption setup, repetition-related overfitting depends on model size, training duration and language sampling strategy.

record.problems: No scaling-law fits, exponent estimates, or compute-optimal allocation analysis; held-out loss trends are presented in plots without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The reported comparisons use a limited multilingual encoder-decoder setting and the authors note pretraining instability for umT5-Large.
record.rows_left_out: To stay within 60 rows, omitted WMT21 Figure 6 score curves, Figure 4 score curves where Table 7 supplies the TyDi averages, Table 5 additional benchmark results, and the per-language breakdowns in Table 7. These are additional downstream evaluations; the retained rows include the Table 3 model-size results, TyDi averages, and the stated repeated-data overfitting conditions.

untested.parts: No power-law fit or assessment across several orders of magnitude with other resources non-bottlenecking.
No small-run law is used to predict larger-run loss.
No loss-minimising parameter/token allocation at fixed compute or compute-scaling exponents.
No architecture comparison at fixed parameter count.
Repeated-data training is examined, but whether its loss follows a power law is not tested.

No quantitative predictive law, larger-scale extrapolation, or measured mapping from pretraining loss to downstream performance. Evidence primarily concerns the direction of average performance changes within tested size series.
No comparison of fitted exponents, compute-optimal splits, fitting procedures, or departures from a fitted single power law.

missing.what: The excluded full-budget umT5-Large model exhibited pretraining instability and underperformed umT5-Base on all metrics. Add a qualitative reversal row; numerical scores are unavailable. The general problems field mentions instability but does not record this downstream reversal.

Fourfold longer Large-model training gives TyDi QA scores of 81.2, 82.8 and 83.1 for temperature 1, temperature 3.33 and UniMax. The temperature baselines improve over Table 7's 80.1 and 82.0. UniMax's 83.1 is below Table 7's 83.3 despite prose claiming improvement across the board; flag this discrepancy and the changed UniMax distribution.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict supports or challenges a power-law form here. The downstream results provide descriptive size trends rather than validated quantitative predictions. Table 3's mT5 columns are reference comparisons; verdicts above rely on the study's own umT5 and controlled sampling experiments. Results explicitly declared in rows_left_out are not duplicated as missing.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fits of held-out loss against parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fit is used to predict larger-run loss.
No fixed-compute optimization of parameter and token allocations.
No controlled depth, width, or architecture comparison at fixed parameter count.
The study evaluates multilingual text pretraining and repetition, but does not test whether a power-law form holds in repeated-data or other training regimes.

The study reports downstream metrics at several model sizes, but does not fit a predictive relationship from pretraining loss to downstream performance or establish extrapolation beyond the tested sizes.
It does not compare fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits across parameter-counting, fitting, or schedule choices; its evidence concerns held-out loss changes under sampling/repetition choices.

relationships.condition: Reported umT5 Small, Base, XL and XXL checkpoints on the five Table 3 benchmarks
relationships.reason: All five benchmark averages increase across these retained sizes; for example, umt5-s-xnli through umt5-xxl-xnli rise from 76.2 to 87.8. This supports directional improvement within the tested range.
relationships.display_finding: All five benchmark averages increased with model size, including XNLI from 76.2 to 87.8.

relationships.condition: TyDi QA language averages, 1.2B–13B parameters, separately under each of the three sampling strategies
relationships.reason: tydi-L-t1 through tydi-XXL-t1 increase 80.1→81.7→82.2; the corresponding temperature-3.33 and UniMax series increase 82.0→83.4→84.0 and 83.3→83.9→84.4.
relationships.display_finding: TyDi QA averages increased from 80.1 to 81.7 to 82.2 under temperature 1, from 82.0 to 83.4 to 84.0 under temperature 3.33, and from 83.3 to 83.9 to 84.4 under UniMax.

relationships.reason: Section 6 footnote 5 explicitly says umT5-Large underperformed umT5-Base on every metric and was excluded; this text-only result, missing from the rows, makes improvement conditional on successful training.
relationships.display_finding: umT5-Large underperformed umT5-Base on every metric and was excluded from evaluation.

relationships.condition: Large models with fourfold longer pretraining under temperature sampling
relationships.reason: Table 2, missing from the rows, reports TyDi QA increases from 80.1 to 81.2 for temperature 1 and from 82.0 to 82.8 for temperature 3.33 relative to tydi-L-t1 and tydi-L-t333.
relationships.display_finding: TyDi QA increased from 80.1 to 81.2 under temperature 1 and from 82.0 to 82.8 under temperature 3.33.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: mT5 and umT5 model-size series on the five Table 3 benchmarks, and the TyDi QA averages across Large, XL, and XXL
reader_labels.reason: Reported downstream scores generally rise across the tested size series; see mt5-s-xnli through umt5-xxl-tydi and tydi-L-t1 through tydi-XXL-um.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: τ = 3.33 repeated-data sampling on Yoruba, especially at larger sizes and longer training
reader_labels.reason: Overfitting is absent at Large but weak at XL, conspicuous at XXL, and appears for Large after around 300,000 steps in the longer run; UniMax shows no reported sign in these curves. See loss2-y-L, loss2-y-XL, loss2-y-XXL, loss3-y-L, and the UniMax comparison rows.
